info.title: KamoCore CLI
info.description: Run KamoCore API Tester suites and UI Tester tracks from your own machine or pipeline, gate a pipeline on SQL and Cache checks, relay requests into a private network, and tell KamoCore about a deploy.

commands.name: agent
commands.description: Let KamoCore send requests into a private network through this machine

options.name: --allow
options.description: A host this agent may send to: localhost:5000, api.local, *.internal, 10.0.0.0/8 (required) (may repeat)

options.name: --name
options.description: What to call this machine in KamoCore. Default: its own name

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Nothing is allowed until you name it with --allow, and the list lives on this machine: KamoCore is shown it, never
asked. The agent sends only to local and private addresses, and never to a link-local or cloud platform one.
The agent serves only the person its access token acts as, in the one workspace that token is for. It opens no
port: it asks KamoCore for work. Stop it with Ctrl+C; revoking the token stops it too. Give it a token of its
own with the scope ApiTesterAgent:write ("API Tester CLI agent") and no other: it opens nothing else.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Run a Cache Tester connection's checks on KamoCore (kamocore cache check) and fail the pipeline when one does not hold

options.name: --connection
options.description: The Cache Tester connection whose checks run (required)

options.name: --check
options.description: Run only this check, switched on or not (repeat, or separate ids with commas). Default: every switched-on check (may repeat)

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write the result as JUnit XML to this file, for the pipeline's test tab

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds and ask KamoCore to stop the run (exit 2). Default: 1800

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
KamoCore runs the checks on its own queue, the same as Run all in the app. The CLI follows the run, prints each check that
did not hold and exits 1 when one did not; a run that was stopped part way or could not run exits 2. What a key holds is
never printed or written. The access token needs the scope CacheTester:write.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Check a branch or pull request against its designs (kamocore check design), and fail the pipeline when asked

options.name: --source
options.description: The Designer code source the scans are sent to (required)

options.name: --branch
options.description: The branch to check. Default: KAMOCORE_BRANCH, the pipeline's variables, else what git says

options.name: --pull-request
options.description: The pull request to check. Default: KAMOCORE_PULL_REQUEST, else the pull request the pipeline builds

options.name: --fail-on
options.description: Fail the pipeline (exit 1) when any of these results is found: broken, missing, unplanned, different, unproven, rules (a break of a rule set to fail)

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
KamoCore compares the latest reading "kamocore scan --source" sent for the branch or pull request with the designs the
code source is matched with. Each function of a design matches, is missing, is unplanned (in the code, not in the design),
differs, is broken (its linked tests fail) or is unproven (no evidence yet). The check fails the pipeline only for the
results --fail-on names, and never while KamoCore cannot check yet. On the Free plan KamoCore answers the counts only.
The access token needs the scope Designer:read.

commands.name: migrations
commands.description: Check the database migrations a change adds for steps that lose data or stop a running release

options.name: --base
options.description: The commit the change started from (default: the last commit's parent)

options.name: --path
options.description: Check every migration under this file or folder instead of the change (may repeat)

options.name: --fail-on
options.description: What fails the check: risky (the default, every flagged step), destructive, or none

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write the result as JUnit XML to this file

options.name: --project
options.description: Tell this project how the check went, so "Can we ship?" shows it. Counts only; needs a token

options.name: --commit
options.description: The commit that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEVERSION

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Reads the EF Core migrations (their Up method) and .sql files the change adds or edits - since --base, else since the last
commit, with what is not committed yet - or every one under --path. Destructive: a dropped table or column, an emptied table,
a DELETE without WHERE. Risky: a rename, a narrowed or changed type, a required column without a default, an index built
without CONCURRENTLY. A step a person accepts on purpose carries "kamocore: allow" in a comment on its line or the line above:
it is still listed, as accepted, and never fails the check. Only the text is read: nothing connects to a database, and no
access token is needed.

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Print a script that completes kamocore's commands and options as you type, for your shell

options.name: --shell
options.description: The shell: bash, zsh, fish or powershell. (required)

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Load it once in your shell's profile. bash: eval "$(kamocore completion --shell bash)". zsh: the same with zsh.
fish: kamocore completion --shell fish | source. PowerShell: kamocore completion --shell powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression.

commands.name: Defaults
commands.description:
kamocore.json in this folder, or in a folder above it up to the repository's root, keeps defaults: a top-level
setting for every command that has the option, an object under a command's name ("run", "ui run") for that
command only. What the command line says wins. The server and the token are never read from the file.

commands.name: deploy
commands.description: Tell KamoCore a service or API was deployed, so it runs the affected suites

options.name: --project
options.description: The project whose API was deployed, by name or id

options.name: --environment
options.description: The environment it was deployed to, by name or id

options.name: --environment-url
options.description: The address it was deployed to (http or https)

options.name: --deploy-id
options.description: The pipeline's own id for this deploy, per environment; told twice, it starts nothing twice

options.name: --version
options.description: The version that was deployed

options.name: --openapi
options.description: The OpenAPI document of what was deployed, compared as a new version of the API

options.name: --changes
options.description: Say which changes the deploy carried: the commits since the last deploy there, from the git history here

options.name: --wait
options.description: Wait until the suites finished; the exit code says how

options.name: --timeout
options.description: With --wait: how long to wait. Default: 1800

options.name: --fail-on-breaking
options.description: With --wait and --openapi: exit 1 when the new version breaks the contract

options.name: --preview
options.description: Say instead that the preview of this pull request is up, built from --commit, so a coding agent's card is verified on it

options.name: --pipeline
options.description: The pipeline's name, shown with the run. Default: BUILD_DEFINITIONNAME

options.name: --pipeline-run
options.description: The pipeline run or build number. Default: BUILD_BUILDNUMBER

options.name: --commit
options.description: The commit that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEVERSION

options.name: --branch
options.description: The branch that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEBRANCHNAME

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
KamoCore runs the suites on its own servers, as a person - whoever the token acts for, or a suite's owner for a
service account - and counts them like any run. With an OpenAPI document it runs the suites the change touches;
without one, or when nothing changed in it, every suite of the project. The access token needs ApiTester:write.
With --changes the CLI asks KamoCore for the commit deployed last to the environment and reads the first-parent
commits since then from the git history in the working directory, each with its commit time. A first deploy, a
shallow checkout that does not reach the last deploy, or a history that commit is no longer in sends the deployed
commit alone. Without --changes KamoCore looks for the changes in the workspace's repository connections.
With --preview <pull request number> --commit <sha> the pipeline says it deployed the preview of a pull request -
the head commit it built, not a merge commit. KamoCore then verifies the coding-agent card waiting on that pull request
by running the card's locked tests on the preview itself. It is only a signal of when: the pull request and its head
commit still come from the repository's signed webhook, nothing matches another commit, no suite of the project runs,
the API's contract is not compared and nothing told here is evidence. The access token needs Boards:write.

commands.name: Environment
commands.description:
KAMOCORE_TOKEN   The access token. It is read only from the environment, never from an option.
KAMOCORE_SERVER  Where KamoCore is. Default: https://www.kamocore.com

commands.name: login
commands.description: Keep a token on this machine, for a person at their own keyboard

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
An environment variable always wins over the kept token, so a pipeline sets KAMOCORE_TOKEN as before and needs no login.

commands.name: logout
commands.description: Forget the token kept on this machine

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --help
options.description: Show this help

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Serve KamoCore to a coding agent as tools, over standard input and output

options.name: --allow-writes
options.description: Offer the tools that change something in KamoCore. Default: read-only

options.name: --allow-hosts
options.description: With --suite or --project: offer running those from this machine, to these hosts only: localhost:5000, api.example.com, *.internal (may repeat)

options.name: --suite
options.description: A suite the agent may run from this machine (may repeat)

options.name: --project
options.description: A project whose suites the agent may run from this machine (may repeat)

options.name: --secret-host
options.description: Give a secret to the agent's runs, for these hosts only: apiKey=localhost:5000, or auth:Staging login=api.example.com (may repeat)

options.name: --secret-env
options.description: Read a secret from another environment variable: apiKey=MY_KEY, or auth:Staging login=MY_TOKEN (may repeat)

options.name: --insecure
options.description: Accept a certificate that cannot be verified

options.name: --run-timeout
options.description: Stop a suite run after this long. Default: 600, at most 3600

options.name: --writes-per-hour
options.description: With --allow-writes: how many changes an hour are taken. Default: 60, at most 600

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Speaks the Model Context Protocol over standard input and output: an agent host starts this command and talks to
it. Standard output carries the protocol and nothing else; what the server says to you goes to the error stream.
It answers hosts that open with a handshake and hosts that send their protocol version with every request.
Without --allow-writes the server only reads, and the tools that change something are not offered at all: running
a suite on KamoCore's servers, filing a bug, reporting a deploy, recording a release, and recording a local run.
The agent can do nothing the access token cannot, so give the token only the scopes the agent needs.
A suite is run from this machine only when you name both the hosts a run may send to (--allow-hosts) and what may
be run (--suite, --project): the agent runs nothing else, whatever the access token reaches, and no tool argument
can add a host or a suite. A local host is named with its port (localhost:5000). Secrets are read from this
machine's environment, and only those you give for a host with --secret-host name=host: each is sent to its hosts
and nowhere else, one given for none is not used at all, and none is ever returned to the agent.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a suite or a project from this machine and report the result

options.name: --suite
options.description: The suite to run, by name or id; a name is looked for in --project when one is given

options.name: --project
options.description: The project to run, every saved request of it, by name or id

options.name: --environment
options.description: The environment to run in, by name or id. Default: the project's default

options.name: --group
options.description: With --project: one test group instead of every request

options.name: --allow-hosts
options.description: The hosts this run may send to, comma separated: api.example.com, localhost:5000, *.internal, 10.0.0.0/8 (may repeat)

options.name: --allow-any-host
options.description: Instead of --allow-hosts: let the run send to any host its suite names

options.name: --secret-env
options.description: Read a secret from another environment variable: apiKey=MY_KEY, or auth:Staging login=MY_TOKEN (may repeat)

options.name: --secret-host
options.description: Give a secret for certain hosts only, so it is sent nowhere else: apiKey=api.example.com, or auth:Staging login=localhost:5000 (may repeat)

options.name: --allow-missing-secrets
options.description: Run although a secret is missing; a step that needs it is not sent

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write the result as JUnit XML

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the result as JSON

options.name: --fail-fast
options.description: Stop at the first step that fails; steps marked to always run still run

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Stop the whole run after this long

options.name: --insecure
options.description: Accept a certificate that cannot be verified

options.name: --report
options.description: What to post back to KamoCore. Default: full

options.name: --affected
options.description: With --project: run only the suites the changes in this git checkout touch; everything runs when KamoCore cannot tell, and it says why. A pull request does this by default

options.name: --base
options.description: With --affected: the commit to compare HEAD with, such as the pull request's merge base. Default: HEAD's parent

options.name: --all
options.description: With --project: run every suite, also in a pull request

options.name: --pipeline
options.description: The pipeline's name, shown with the run. Default: BUILD_DEFINITIONNAME

options.name: --pipeline-run
options.description: The pipeline run or build number. Default: BUILD_BUILDNUMBER

options.name: --commit
options.description: The commit that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEVERSION

options.name: --branch
options.description: The branch that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEBRANCHNAME

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Secrets never come from KamoCore. A secret variable named apiKey is read from the environment variable
KAMOCORE_SECRET_APIKEY, a sign-in named Staging login from KAMOCORE_AUTH_STAGING_LOGIN (upper case, anything but
letters and digits an underscore). A sign-in that uses a login request signs in from this machine instead.
The access token needs the scope ApiTester:read to read the suite and ApiTester:write to post the result.
Whoever may edit a project decides what its suites send, so a run is told on this machine where it may send:
name the hosts with --allow-hosts and nothing goes anywhere else - no request, no secret. --allow-any-host lets
the suite decide instead. A link-local or cloud platform address is never sent to. A secret given for certain hosts
with --secret-host is sent to those hosts only, whatever a suite asks; one given for none goes where the run may send.
--affected reads the changed files from git here (HEAD against --base, else against HEAD's parent, plus files not yet committed) and asks
KamoCore which suites they touch, from the Designer's code readings and the links between catalog components, endpoints, requests and
suites. No AI decides it. The access token needs Designer:read as well as the ApiTester scopes. When KamoCore cannot tell, every
suite of the project runs and the reason is printed. A shallow checkout without HEAD's parent needs --base or a deeper fetch. With several suites, --junit and --json write one file per suite: the first
under the name given, the next ones with -2, -3 before the extension.

commands.name: runner
commands.description: Claim the steps of runs you started and start your agent host on each, with the step's own credential

options.name: --run
options.description: Claim only the steps of this run. Default: any run you started

options.name: --host
options.description: The program to start for each step - your agent host (required)

options.name: --host-arg
options.description: An argument for the host, in order; repeat it for each (may repeat)

options.name: --once
options.description: Stop after one step

options.name: --beat
options.description: Seconds between the heartbeats sent while a host works. Default: 300

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Runs with your own access token (KAMOCORE_TOKEN, a kamo_pat_ token with Boards:write) - only the person who started a run may claim its
steps. For each step KamoCore opens it hands over the step's card credential, in this answer only; the runner starts --host with it in
KAMOCORE_TOKEN, the card's key in KAMOCORE_CARD and its branch in KAMOCORE_BRANCH, says it is alive while the host works, and claims the
next step when the host ends. Neither token is ever printed: both are taken out of everything the host and the runner write.
It stops when KamoCore refuses the token or the claim, after one step with --once, or when you stop it. A step's credential ends on its own.

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Read the services your files describe and the application in your code, and send them to a Designer code source

options.name: --dry
options.description: Print exactly what would be sent, and send nothing

options.name: --out
options.description: Write what would be sent to a file

options.name: --source
options.description: The Designer code source to send the reading to

options.name: --include-openapi
options.description: Also send whole OpenAPI documents, not only the endpoints they list

options.name: --root
options.description: The folder to read. Default: the working directory

options.name: --commit
options.description: The commit that was read; for a pull request its head commit. Default: KAMOCORE_COMMIT, the pipeline's variables, else what git says

options.name: --branch
options.description: The branch that was read; for a pull request its source branch. Default: KAMOCORE_BRANCH, the pipeline's variables, else what git says

options.name: --default-branch
options.description: The repository's default branch. Default: KAMOCORE_DEFAULT_BRANCH, CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH, else the branch origin/HEAD names

options.name: --pull-request
options.description: The pull request whose head was read. Default: KAMOCORE_PULL_REQUEST, else the pull request the pipeline builds

options.name: --manifests-only
options.description: Read only manifests and API descriptions, no source code

options.name: --no-node
options.description: Never start node: read TypeScript lexically

options.name: --layers
options.description: Map only these layers, comma separated: backend, web. Overrides the source's scope

options.name: --include
options.description: Map only paths matching these globs, comma separated (** any folders, * within a name). Overrides the source's scope

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Leave out paths matching these globs, comma separated. Overrides the source's scope

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Only names are read: services, images, connections and endpoints from compose, Helm and Kubernetes files,
Dockerfiles, project files, package.json, go.mod, pom.xml, Gradle builds, pyproject.toml, setup.py, Pipfile,
requirements files, OpenAPI documents and the names in settings files. Never a value, an environment value, a
secret or code. .env files, keys, certificates and secret folders are skipped, nothing is run, and every name that
looks like a secret is left out. --dry prints exactly what would be sent.
From the code it reads the application's names: C# endpoints (minimal APIs and controllers), handlers, background
jobs and the tables their contexts map, parsed into syntax trees and never built; Java endpoints (Spring, Jakarta REST,
Micronaut), services, JPA entities and repositories, clients, listeners and their security and validation annotations;
Python routes (FastAPI, Flask, Django), models (SQLAlchemy, Django), services, tasks, dependencies and decorators -
Java and Python read by KamoCore's own readers, with no JDK or Python needed; the requests and message topics that
leave the repository; and a web app's routes, screens, tabs, actions and the requests they send. TypeScript is read
with your repository's own typescript package through node when both are there - the CLI installs nothing - else
lexically, marked low confidence. Each source file is read, turned into names, paths, symbols and line numbers, and let
go: no line of code is kept or sent. --manifests-only reads no code; --no-node never starts node.
In a git repository the files are those git tracks; elsewhere the folder is walked, never following a link out
of it and never into node_modules, bin, obj or .git. The access token needs the scope Designer:write to send.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a SQL Tester project on KamoCore (kamocore sql run) and fail the pipeline when a case fails

options.name: --project
options.description: The SQL Tester project to run (required)

options.name: --environment
options.description: The environment to run against. Default: the project's default environment

options.name: --group
options.description: Run only the cases of this test group

options.name: --case
options.description: Run only this case (repeat, or separate ids with commas) (may repeat)

options.name: --chained
options.description: Run the cases one at a time in their chain order, passing extracted values on

options.name: --failing-only
options.description: Run only the cases whose latest run failed

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write the result as JUnit XML to this file, for the pipeline's test tab

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds and ask KamoCore to stop the run (exit 2). Default: 1800

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
KamoCore runs the cases on its own queue against the environment the project keeps, under the project's safety policy -
the same as Run all in the app. The CLI follows the run, prints each case that failed and exits 1 when one did; a case
that could not run (a plan limit, a stop) or a run that could not finish exits 2. No row and no value an assertion saw
is printed or written. The access token needs the scope SqlTester:write.

options.name: --site

options.name: --track

options.name: --tag

options.name: --environment

options.name: --schedule

options.name: --parameter

options.name: --secret-env

options.name: --browser

options.name: --retry

options.name: --api-capture
options.description: Send the API calls of each track that passed to this API Tester browser sync connection, to review and make a suite of

options.name: --allow-hosts
options.description: With a card agent's credential: the host its locked tracks run against, with its port: localhost:3000 (may repeat)

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write the result as JUnit XML to this file, for the pipeline's test tab

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Stop after this many seconds: the running track is stopped and reported, the rest are not run (exit 2). Default: 1800

options.name: --pipeline
options.description: The pipeline's name, shown with the run. Default: BUILD_DEFINITIONNAME

options.name: --pipeline-run
options.description: The pipeline run or build number. Default: BUILD_BUILDNUMBER

options.name: --commit
options.description: The commit that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEVERSION

options.name: --branch
options.description: The branch that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEBRANCHNAME

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print failures and the totals only

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Each track runs here, with Playwright, exactly as KamoCore would replay it: the same steps, selectors, time limits and
allowed origins, after the environment's sign-in. Sites in a private network work, since the browser is on this
machine. Every run is reported to KamoCore, where it counts like any other run - the track's last result, flaky
tracks, a schedule waiting for its turn, linked cards and "Can we ship?". A track that fails exits 1; a sign-in that
failed, a track that could not run or was stopped, or a run KamoCore could not record exits 2. A track held in
quarantine is run and reported but never fails the gate. The access token needs the scopes UiTester:read and UiTester:write.
Secrets never come from KamoCore. A secret named "password" is read from KAMOCORE_SECRET_PASSWORD, the recorded
password {{secret}} from KAMOCORE_SECRET_SECRET; --secret-env password=STAGING_PASSWORD reads it from another variable.
Only the secrets a step types are read, and none of them is printed, written or reported.
--api-capture turns what the UI does into API tests: the fetch and XHR calls each passed track's steps make (not the
sign-in's) go to an API Tester browser sync connection as a recording. API Tester keeps the calls to its approved
origins, drops credentials and secret fields, and holds the rest for review; open the printed address to review it and
make a suite. The connection must be the token's person's own, so use a personal access token with ApiTester:read and
ApiTester:write as well. Sending never changes the gate's result.
With a card agent's credential (kamo_agt_) it runs the card's locked tracks by id, through the card's own local-run plan, against the host you
name with --allow-hosts only, with values only from this machine's environment. Such a run is a hint: it never counts as a round, uses no
try and is reported nowhere.

options.name: --server
options.description: Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com

options.name: --token-env
options.description: The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN

Show this help
Any access token may ask, and asking changes nothing. The token itself is never printed - only its kind, its name, its
workspace, its scopes and when it ends - so a pipeline can check its setup before it runs anything.
